## 末日警告并非人工智能浪潮下的唯一威胁：英美居民还在抗议数据中心

**末日警告并非人工智能浪潮下的唯一威胁：英美居民还在抗议数据中心**

*       *   ![Image 2](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/ws/160/cpsprodpb/2d88/live/aec02270-b0e6-11f1-bc1f-3f186ca4140c.png.webp)

    *   Author, 费萨尔·伊斯兰（Faisal Islam）
    *   Role, BBC经济编辑

*   Published 2026年9月16日

*   阅读时间: 6 分钟

数据中心里有一种诡异的低沉嗡鸣声。在那里，数以万计的晶片每秒进行数万亿次运算，推动着人工智能（artificial intelligence, AI；人工智慧）革命的车轮前进。

这些晶片为全球各地向先进人工智能模型发出的查询提供动力，生成文字、图像和视频。

它们的运算，本质上是构成晶片（芯片）的微型硅晶体管不断开合的过程，实际上是无声的。但与所有电脑一样，为这一过程提供动力的大量电力，几乎每一瓦最终都以热能的形式散出，而你听到的声音，正是数千台风扇缓慢运转的嗡鸣——它们的作用是防止热量烧毁成排的服务器机架。

视乎场地规模，你还可能听到变电站中输送电力的变压器发出的嗡嗡声。

](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/ws/640/cpsprodpb/14b9/live/89e5d0e0-b117-11f1-a540-61c3f7fc4e6c.jpg.webp)

图像来源，Getty Images

图像加注文字，位于英格兰赫特福德郡（Hertfordshire）的这座正在建设中的谷歌（Google）数据中心等设施，正在英国各地变得越来越普遍。

近日来，关于人类面临威胁的惊人警告甚嚣尘上，但真正引发反弹的却是这些低沉的嗡鸣声——这场反弹正在美国发酵，如今已威胁到其国会中期选举，并可能跨越大西洋蔓延至英国。

在美国，对数据中心的反对声音在政治左翼中最为公开。民主党参议员伯尼·桑德斯（Bernie Sanders）呼吁暂停一切新的数据中心建设。

桑德斯告诉我：“人们环顾四周，忧心忡忡——担心这项技术发展得有多快，担心自己对它的掌控力有多小，担心数据中心会如何影响自己所在社区的电价和水资源使用。”

全球人工智能竞赛正以矽谷（Silicon Valley）的最高速度飞速发展，但有可能即将因一些非常本地化的政治和环境问题而受阻。

## 一场有毒辩论

在美国，盖洛普（Gallup）今年5月发布的民调显示，在自己所在区域建数据中心，比建核电站更不受欢迎。就数据中心而言，71%的受访者表示反对，其中48%强烈反对；核电站方面，53%表示反对，其中34%强烈反对。

这种不受欢迎程度在过去两年中不断加深，一些民调显示，半数美国人支持全面暂停数据中心建设。

在英国，部分此类开发项目也遭到了反对——从白金汉郡（Buckinghamshire）、伯克郡（Berkshire）到伦敦东部的红砖巷（Brick Lane），当地居民担心自己所在区域将受到负面影响。

在红砖巷，一个很可能为伦敦金融城（City of London）高频交易商提供服务的数据中心计划，遭到了部分人士的反对，他们更希望看到伦敦东区建设更多社会住房和本地商业项目。

与此同时，在英格兰各郡，对数据中心的巨大需求正带来扩大供给的压力——从斯劳（Slough）一路向绿树成荫的乡村地带延伸。

英国拥有全球第三多的数据中心，中国第二，美国第一。

回到美国，这种反弹也反映在了即将参加11月关键选举的政治人物的言论中。

图像来源，AFP via Getty Images

图像加注文字，能源和水资源方面的压力引发了当地的抗议活动。

这场反弹显然在左翼民主党人中更为明显，但反对数据中心的情绪在共和党支持者中同样清晰可见。一些市议会因其数据中心政策而在选举中被赶下台，而一些州——无论是共和党主导的红州还是民主党主导的蓝州——正在提出禁令。

去年，新泽西州（New Jersey）和弗吉尼亚州（Virginia）的民主党州长之所以能够当选，部分原因正是民众对电价上涨的反弹——而电价上涨被指与数据中心的建设和营运有关。

类似的故事层出不穷：当地小镇居民被要求为新数据中心供电所需的基础设施买单，眼睁睁看着能源账单飙升；或者发现本已紧张的供水进一步减少。由于美国能源系统在地方层面运作，因此帐单上的影响可能立竿见影。

由于美国国会两院的控制权都悬而未决，这种高度地方化的反对力量的规模可能会成为中期选举的决定性因素，进而影响美国政策的走向以及唐纳德·特朗普（Donald Trump；川普）的总统任期。

## 令人眼花撩乱的翻转

今年3月，七大科技巨头的首席执行官与特朗普一同出席签署了“纳税人保护承诺”（Ratepayer Protection Pledge），承诺将“自建、引入或购买”自身所需的能源，并确保成本不会转嫁给“普通家庭”。该承诺不具约束力。

图像来源，Getty Images

图像加注文字，这份承诺几乎没有说服人们接受在自己所在区域建设数据中心。

对一些人来说，这显然还不够。新泽西州和弗吉尼亚州（后者拥有全球规模最大的数据中心集聚区）的新任民主党州长走得更远，通过立法强制为数据中心设立新的能源资费标准，并要求披露能源和水的使用情况。

也许这一切最有力的象征，是德克萨斯州（Texas）亲特朗普的共和党参议院候选人肯·帕克斯顿（Ken Paxton）。他抨击数据中心，在竞选中反对给予其税收减免，并提议：如果相关技术“赋能了损害儿童安全的人工智能聊天机器人”，这些设施的营运商应承担刑事责任。

德克萨斯州曾是最亲商、最亲数据中心、最亲能源产业的州，曾为争夺这类设施展开激烈竞争。例如，它赢得了埃隆·马斯克（Elon Musk）旗下 SpaceX 人工智能巨头数十亿美元搬迁投资中的大部分，用于生产人工智能晶片。

图像来源，Getty Images

图像加注文字，肯·帕克斯顿对人工智能采取了强硬立场。

这是一次令人眩晕的转向。人工智能晶片制造商英伟达（Nvidia；辉达）的负责人黄仁勋（Jensen Huang）今年8月登上社交媒体，力陈数据中心是美国再工业化的关键推手。其他科技巨头的首席执行官没有跟进，这或许显示此举在公众眼中颇具争议。

然而，美国的经验表明，谈论对国家经济的整体益处，或潜在的癌症治愈能力，并不总是能引起当地民众的共鸣。数据中心令人感到不安的部分原因在于，这里缺乏真正意义上的常驻员工。

虽然建筑业提供了大量的就业机会，但一个运作正常的数据中心通常只需要数十名员工，即使是规模最大的新建数据中心也只有几百名员工。

要求当地居民接受噪音、彻夜不熄的安保照明，以及对当地能源和水资源供应的压力，并告诉他们这是为了国家利益，这固然容易。但当人工智能公司估值即将突破万亿美元大关，却又预计会造成大规模失业，许多人质疑这项技术是否会将人类从地球上抹去时，要说服他们接受这些措施就难上加难了。

## 关键基础设施

这些争论已经跨越大西洋。在英国斯劳——欧洲最大的数据中心集群——超过500人签署了一份请愿书，称该镇“不应成为一场试验”。他们质疑该镇是否真的从中受益，并要求暂停镇上的数据中心开发。

当地居民抱怨，数据中心产生的热量让本就酷热的夏季气温雪上加霜。有一个项目的选址原本规划用于建设1000套住房，但作为地方议会清偿债务的一部分，被卖给了一家数据中心公司。

回到红砖巷，前工党上议院议员波拉·乌丁女男爵（Baroness Pola Uddin）表示：“我理解建设数据中心的必要性，但必须妥善考虑当地居民的健康与福祉——他们在这里生活、呼吸、上学。我们必须考虑选择更工业化的区域。”

图像来源，AFP via Getty Images

图像加注文字，红砖巷的抗议者们不满他们的社区被利用来服务市政府。

工党政府去年将数据中心列为“关键国家基础设施”（Critical National Infrastructure），这是其加快数据中心部署战略的一部分。

政府认为，数据中心是公共服务的基石，对吸引投资、让英国在全球经济中保持竞争力至关重要。

政府提出的论据是国家经济利益，但政治上的挑战在于当地民众是否愿意忍受。新工党政府上台后的第一批行动之一，就是支持一个位于白金汉郡的数据中心项目——该项目因建在绿化带上而屡遭地方议会拒绝。

大臣们批准了该项目，但随后抗议人士通过众筹发起诉讼，以未考虑环境影响为由提出质疑。政府承认存在错误，撤销了自己的批准，开发商最终承认需要与议会达成具有约束力的清洁能源义务协议。获胜的倡议组织福克斯格洛夫（Foxglove）誓言将把精力重新集中到挑战英国各地其他数据中心项目上。

水是活动人士关注的另一个领域。科技行业辩称，如果考虑到例如管道渗漏损失的水量，他们的用水需求其实并不算大。

在提交给下议院一个委员会的意见书中，行业组织英国水务协会（Water UK）批评政府的人工智能增长战略“对水只字未提”。“似乎存在一种假设，认为这个国家的水资源永远足以满足其经济需求。没有什么比这更离谱的了。”

英国近期扩建数据中心的努力，大多瞄准经过战略性筛选的区域——选址综合考量其对经济的潜在贡献、可供开发的棕地，以及与能源电网和发电设施的现有连接。这些区域被称为“人工智能增长区”（AI Growth zones）。

但即使在这些地方，增长与环境之间的政治平衡也导致内阁内部的拖延。提赛德（Teesside）的一个项目曾引发大臣们之间的拉锯战——争论该地块应用于低碳氢能源项目，还是一座大型新人工智能数据中心。最终，数据中心胜出。

## 环境妥协

矽谷的科技巨头们已经承认，大规模人工智能数据中心的能源需求将导致应对气候变化的进展放缓。英伟达的黄仁勋去年告诉我，当务之急是人工智能本身的发明与部署，他并声称这项技术本身可以帮助解决气候变化问题。“这是在生产智能——还有什么比这更有价值、更重要？”

在英国，仍存在一个根本性问题：一项计划到2030年将现有数据中心容量扩大两倍、达到6吉瓦（gigawatt, GW）持续容量的方案，其电力需求能否与净零排放计划相协调。

预计政府很快将在一份《国家政策声明》（National Policy Statement, NPS）中概述其针对地方政府的数据中心政策，明确哪些类型的项目属于“国家重大项目”，因而有资格由政府加快审批。

自开始起草这份政策声明以来，首相已经换人，围绕这一议题的政治温度也发生了变化。

首相安迪·伯纳姆（Andy Burnham）承诺实现“每个邮编区域都有增长”，而数据中心或许有助于兑现这一承诺。然而，政府在其中扮演的主导角色，也是国家权力集中化的明显例证——这与伯纳姆向地方政府下放更多权力的愿望背道而驰。

这一点，再加上绿党（Green Party）呼吁暂停建设数据中心所带来的挑战，会不会改变安迪·伯纳姆的想法？

## “美国脑袋”

威斯敏斯特的一些人认为，这个议题上存在一种“美国脑袋”（America brain）现象——仅仅因为它在美国是个问题，人们就认为英国也同样如此。

他们表示，当英国正努力达到6吉瓦这一目标时，美国2030年的雄心至少是这个数字的20倍，一些单体超大型项目的规模甚至超过英国的总规划容量。

他们说，对当地电价的影响并不相同——尽管这在一定程度上是因为英国的能源价格本来就更高。

对英国而言，还有一个关乎数据主权的重要论据：避免在支撑服务经济大面积领域的信息技术基础设施上，完全依赖美国或其他国家。

有人谈到，需要汲取本世纪初社交媒体和互联网发展的教训——英国当时未能捕捉到随之而来的经济和政治权力红利，主要是这些技术的使用者，而非制造者。

一位大臣告诉我：“这一次（在人工智能上），我们必须做对，但前提是拥有一定水平的数据基础设施。”英国的雄心被视为相对适度——目标是到2030年，在国民保健服务体系（NHS）、国家安全和金融服务领域实现持续的人工智能应用。

这种“切身利害”的论调在人工智能实验室中得到了呼应。一些有影响力的声音认为，他们的模型对社会的影响将如此深远，以至于会从根本上影响政府征税的能力，尤其是对劳动征税。他们的未来学家畅想着经济中现金流被彻底打乱的图景。实体数据中心或许会成为向这场革命的收益征税的少数途径之一。

在美国，一些曾竭力欢迎数据中心的政客，如今表示自己已经倒戈。税收优惠正在变成税务要求。美国小镇的这种反弹或许具有其独特的美国背景，但也在全球范围内引起了共鸣。

title: Can Human Rights Survive the Era of Great-Power Competition?

Pro-democracy protesters in the Mong Kok district of Hong Kong, Oct. 19, 2014. Photo credit: r-monochrome

_THE JAPAN TIMES
July 20, 2026_

**By Michael Judge**

_When I [first interviewed](https://michaeljudge.substack.com/p/what-happens-to-freedom-deferred) Maya Wang in 2024, China’s crackdown on Hong Kong had entered its fourth year, reshaping the global debate on authoritarianism. Since then, wars, geopolitical rivalry and economic competition have increasingly eclipsed human rights as the world’s defining concern._

_As Human Rights Watch’s deputy Asia director, Wang has become one of the leading figures documenting abuses in China, especially in Hong Kong, Xinjiang and Tibet. Her investigations into mass surveillance, digital authoritarianism and the persecution of ethnic and religious minorities have helped shape international understanding of human rights in the 21st century._

_When we met again at Human Rights Watch’s Tokyo office earlier this month, I asked how human rights have fared in an era increasingly defined by great-power competition — and if she still believes there are reasons for hope._

_— MJ_

**MJ: The last time we spoke, Hong Kong dominated international headlines. Looking back now, what does Hong Kong tell us about where China and the international human rights movement are today?**

**MW:**Actually, I think Hong Kong is a good place to start, because if you think about where we are now with human rights in Hong Kong and its repressive [national security law](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/03/24/asia-pacific/politics/hong-kong-police-phone-computer-passwords/), Hong Kong benefited from that period not long ago when people believed societies like China could liberalize through trade. I think that entire dream is now over.

Hong Kong is on a geopolitical fault line. The national security law, enacted in 2020 and expanded through Hong Kong’s [Article 23 legislation](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2024/03/19/asia-pacific/politics/hong-kong-article-23/) in 2024, also marked the beginning of China’s use of national security laws to shape its interactions with — and influence beyond — its borders. In many ways, Hong Kong is not just a small place. What happens to it tells us something about the future.

I don’t think human rights have simply become marginalized. The international human rights system was a product of World War II. The institutions that came out of that period, including the World Trade Organization, are now all being rethought. There’s pushback against globalization and neoliberalism, both at the popular level and at the government level. The imposition of tariffs marks the end of the “free trade is always good” era.

When China joined the WTO, labor rights were essentially stripped out of trade. Human rights were moved into institutions with very little enforcement power. But legislation like the [Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2021/12/09/world/politics-diplomacy-world/us-house-uyghur-bill/) in the United States adds human rights back into trade.

If democracies adopt legislation like that, they are essentially creating standards for participation in international commerce. Human rights become part of economic policy again.

So while governments today often treat human rights as a lower priority, the reshaping of the international order presents an opportunity. Democracies could seize it — or miss it.

**I used to work for The Wall Street Journal, a paper that has long promoted “free markets and free people.” In places like China, the idea was that if you liberalized markets, politics would follow. People even talked about Hong Kong becoming a Trojan horse. Instead, China became the Trojan horse.**

Exactly. Hong Kong was the Trojan horse that allowed China to enter global trade. China’s political economy is built upon what some scholars call a “low-rights economy.” Communities can be displaced without adequate compensation. Workers cannot organize independent unions. Migrant workers remain second-class citizens.

How do democracies compete with a system that doesn’t bear those social costs? If democracies build those costs back into trade, then they’re leveling the playing field. Human rights are not separate from economics.

**How do artificial intelligence and AI-enabled surveillance fit into that? Does AI simply make authoritarian governments more powerful?**

The issue isn’t only surveillance. Chinese technology develops within a regulatory environment that privileges the collection of data without safeguards. It privileges monitoring and control. It’s not only about whether the government orders companies to do something. It’s about the system those companies emerge from.

Many countries now use both Chinese and Western technology. The key question is whether they have strong privacy laws, transparency requirements and accountability. American companies also collect enormous amounts of data. The difference is that they operate in societies where they can still be investigated, criticized and regulated.

In Europe, for example, Chinese technology still has to comply with the European Union’s strict [General Data Protection Regulation](https://gdpr-info.eu/) law, which sets rigorous standards for how companies collect, store and use personal data. Strong privacy rules make it much harder for those technologies to replicate the surveillance model used inside China. So while Chinese technology is spreading rapidly, regulatory frameworks still matter.

**It doesn’t bode well when the president of the United States is constantly attacking regulations and the foundations of international law. Doesn’t that encourage authoritarian governments to do the same?**

American technology companies already operate in an environment with very limited federal privacy regulation. The United States developed what many scholars call surveillance capitalism.

China has state-led surveillance. The United States has surveillance capitalism. Both raise profound questions about privacy. But they are not equivalent. In China, technology companies are actively recruited into a system of state surveillance. In the United States, you can still expose companies, criticize them publicly and hold them accountable. That distinction matters.

**Myanmar seems to have disappeared from international attention. Are the human rights violations of countries like Myanmar and North Korea falling off the map?**

I think the larger issue is that U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin are all sending the same message: Hard power is what matters. Build your economy. Build your military. Protect yourself. That’s the real game. I think that’s a form of international gaslighting.

For countries like Japan, Canada or Australia, international norms matter enormously. Yes, Myanmar and North Korea receive less attention. But that’s because the world has collectively shifted toward realpolitik.

Human rights emerged after World War II because the world witnessed the horrors of Nazi Germany. The question now is whether we have to experience something comparable again before people recognize why those institutions exist.

Young people in Thailand, Myanmar and Hong Kong understand human rights because they’ve had to fight for them. Sadly, people who grow up inside long-established democracies often take them for granted.

**Japan is reevaluating its security in the region because confidence in the Japan-U.S. alliance has weakened. But what role should it play in promoting human rights and defending democratic ideals?**

China views ideology as a security issue. Xi has made that perfectly clear. Document No. 9, a confidential 2013 Chinese Communist Party directive warning against the influence of Western democratic ideas, identifies democracy, universal values and the rule of law as ideological threats.

Ironically, democracies often don’t think of democracy as something requiring active defense. Japan should invest not only in military and economic security but also in protecting democratic values.

My colleagues and I at Human Rights Watch have proposed an Asia Democracy Fund. Human rights defenders across Asia have become increasingly vulnerable. Democracies could pool resources to support them. . . .

**People often forget that the 1989 Tiananmen movement wasn’t only students; workers also played an enormous role. As AI and automation replace workers, do ordinary people risk losing political power?**

The traditional idea of workers has changed. People no longer work together in one factory their entire lives. Gig workers are isolated. Hannah Arendt wrote that totalitarianism thrives on atomized people, and automation can deepen that isolation.

But new forms of solidarity are emerging. One of the brightest examples in China is feminism. Many highly educated young women increasingly recognize the structural inequalities they face, and because of that they often sympathize with many other human rights causes. They’ve played leading roles in movements ranging from the [White Paper](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2022/11/28/asia-pacific/china-blank-sheet-protest-symbol/) protests [the 2022 demonstrations against COVID-19 restrictions] to animal-rights campaigns.

Every movement creates new activists. There’s reason for hope, even in what might feel like hopeless times.

_Michael Judge is Opinion editor of The Japan Times. This interview was edited for length and clarity._

content:
华盛顿 —

第十三届北京香山论坛9月15日至17日在北京举行。中国官方媒体对论坛进行密集报道，着重强调其规模、国际代表性以及北京为全球安全治理提供“理念和方案”的角色。相比之下，路透社、法国国际广播电台等国际媒体的报道更为有限，关注点也明显不同：它们将论坛置于美中战略竞争、台海与南中国海紧张局势，以及中国试图扩大国际安全话语权的背景下观察。

**中国官方叙事：开放包容与“全球安全治理”**

中国官方媒体的报道首先突出论坛的规模和国际参与度，将其描述为一个日益重要、开放包容的国际安全对话平台。

据中国国防部发布的消息，本届论坛共有来自100多个国家、地区和国际组织的官方代表、专家学者和观察员等约2000人出席，其中包括多名国防部长和军队总长级官员。论坛主题为“凝聚稳定共识，同促安全治理”，议程包括国际秩序、地区安全、全球南方和新兴技术等议题。

香山论坛创办于2006年，最初是一个主要由专家学者参加、每两年举行一次的“二轨”防务交流活动。2014年第五届论坛开始邀请各国防务官员和军方领导人与会，并升级为官方与学术界共同参与的“一轨半”安全对话平台。此后，论坛规模和国际参与度逐步扩大，但其间曾因疫情等原因中断，并非每年连续举行。

在有关本届论坛的报道中，中国官媒和地方官方媒体反复强调“共同安全”“全球南方”“人类命运共同体”以及“国际公共安全产品”等概念，突出中国作为全球安全治理参与者、建设者和协调者的形象。

中国地方官方媒体“[上观新闻](https://news.qq.com/rain/a/20260914A0CKAR00)”刊登的一篇文章则更直接地将论坛与中国国际影响力上升联系起来。文章援引北京香山论坛秘书处前学术主任赵小卓的话说，在“特朗普2.0”时代，美国的公信力在国内和盟友中受到冲击，而中国倡导的和平、合作与共赢理念“优势不断凸显”。

这些报道构成了一套相对一致的官方叙事：面对战争延宕、大国竞争和国际秩序动荡，中国试图以相对稳定、包容和重视发展的安全理念，为现有国际治理体系提供不同于西方的选择。

**国际媒体：从地区紧张局势观察论坛**

与中国官方报道相比，国际媒体较少把重点放在论坛自身的规模和议程上，而是更多将其视为观察中国军事外交和地区战略意图的窗口。

[路透社](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/chinese-defence-forum-set-open-amid-roiling-regional-tensions-2026-09-14/)9月14日发表题为《中国防务论坛将在地区紧张局势动荡之际开幕》(Chinese defense forum set to open amid roiling regional tensions)的报道。文章开篇即把论坛置于台湾、南中国海争端和美国对亚洲安全承诺受到质疑的背景下，并指出中国可能借助论坛宣传由亚洲国家主导地区安全事务的主张。

不过，报道也援引布鲁金斯学会东亚政治与安全问题专家帕特里夏·金(Patricia Kim)的话说，一些亚洲国家虽然对美国的长期安全承诺存在疑虑，但中国在南中国海等问题上的强势行为，也限制了北京借机扩大地区影响力的能力。

董军9月16日在开幕式上警告，各国应警惕“潜藏的霸权主义、军国主义和历史修正主义”，并反对可能损害地区整体利益的“挑衅行径”。他没有直接点名美国、日本或其他国家。

[路透社](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/china-defence-minister-urges-an-end-provocative-acts-open-security-forum-2026-09-16/)在9月16日的后续报道中指出，这些言论可能被视为对日本的含蓄批评，但同时注意到，董军并未直接抨击美国及其地区盟友。这种相对克制的措辞，正值中国国家主席习近平预计赴华盛顿与美国总统特朗普举行峰会前夕。

法国国际广播电台则把董军有关“军国主义”的警告与近期中日关系恶化联系起来。日本共同社援引日中关系消息人士报道，去年参加论坛的日本防卫省防卫研究所研究人员本届未获邀请，日本驻华使馆武官也没有与会。与此同时，日本前首相鸠山由纪夫等民间人士获邀参加。

这一安排与中国官方突出论坛“开放包容”的叙事形成对照，也使日本在本届论坛中的缺席成为国际媒体观察中日安全关系的一个切入点。

与此同时，西方媒体报道还特别关注美国和中国之间的战略关系。

路透社的报道指出，美国五角大楼由负责中国、台湾和蒙古事物的首席主任辛西娅·“赞西”·卡拉斯(Cynthia “Xanthi” Carras)带队，显示美方的参会层级将高于去年由美国驻华使馆国防武官出席的安排。不过，战争部没有回应美国之音(VOA)有关卡拉斯出席本届香山论坛的置评请求。战争部长办公室负责印太事务的发言人梅根·格林(Megan Greeene)在一封给VOA的电邮中说，“对此没有评论可提供。”

**香山论坛与香格里拉对话**

国际媒体经常把北京香山论坛与每年在新加坡举行的香格里拉对话联系起来。香格里拉对话由英国国际战略研究所(IISS)主办，长期以来是美国及其印太盟友阐述地区安全政策的重要平台；香山论坛则由中国军事科学院和中国国际战略学会主办，更集中地呈现北京的安全理念和外交议程。

路透社将香山论坛形容为中国主导、议程安排较为严密的防务对话平台，与讨论和交锋相对开放的香格里拉对话形成对照。两者并非制度上相互排斥的论坛，但在议程设置、参会阵容和政策话语方面，确实反映出中国与美国及其盟友对印太安全秩序的不同理解。

美国战争部长皮特·海格塞斯(Pete Hegseth)今年5月在香格里拉对话上对中国持续扩大军事力量表示警觉，并敦促美国的亚洲盟友增加国防投入。不过，与此前相比，他对中国的措辞相对克制，同时强调美国仍寻求维持美中军事沟通与战略稳定。

**对中国的角色描述不同**

在中国官方叙事中，北京是多边主义、共同安全和全球南方利益的维护者，香山论坛则是中国向世界提供的一项“公共安全产品”。在国际媒体的观察框架中，中国既是国际安全治理的参与者，也是试图重塑规则和扩大话语权的大国；北京宣示的和平与合作理念，还需要同其在台湾海峡、南中国海以及对日关系中的实际行为相互检验。

中国官方媒体新华社9月16日的报道援引国防部部长董军的发言，称中国军队愿与各国军队“共同践行全球安全倡议”，“增强共同安全国际协同”。

《解放军报》则称中国“集中体现中国在冲突纷争中坚守和平之道、在治理困局中探索共赢之策的责任担当，”赋予中国一个全球治理的角色。

值得注意的是，董军在本届论坛上避免直接点名美国，显示北京在习近平预期访美前有意控制对美批评的强度。但论坛有关“霸权主义”“军国主义”和多极秩序的表述也显示，中美在地区安全架构和国际秩序上的根本分歧并未消失。

title: Japan's Takaichi set to signal policy continuity in cabinet reshuffle
summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi holds a press conference at the Prime Minister’s Office, as cabinet support falls, following the close of the 221st extraordinary session of the Diet, in Tokyo, Japan, July 27, 2026. David Mareuil/Pool
content:
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi holds a press conference at the Prime Minister’s Office, as cabinet support falls, following the close of the 221st extraordinary session of the Diet, in Tokyo, Japan, July 27, 2026. David Mareuil/Pool via REUTERS/ File Photo [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/pm-takaichi-holds-press-conference-as-cabinet-support-falls/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMjlNTUFTT0pYTA%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

*   Summary

*   Takaichi seen reappointing Finance Minister Katayama
*   PM's reflationist ally Kiuchi seen keeping post, Yomiuri says
*   Lack of big change signals policy continuity
*   New line-up suggests little change to Takaichi's spending plans

TOKYO, Sept 17 (Reuters) - Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is set to retain key ministers in a cabinet ​reshuffle on Thursday, while looking to shore up political support to push through her flagship spending plans amid jittery ‌financial markets.

In her first reshuffle since taking office last October, Takaichi is likely to retain Satsuki Katayama as finance minister, [sources have told Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/japan-pm-keep-finance-minister-cabinet-reshuffle-mainichi-reports-2026-09-03/), a move that will ensure continuity in Japan's exchange-rate policy.

Make sense of global markets with the Trading Day newsletter. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/trading-day/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fasia-pacific%2Fjapans-takaichi-set-signal-policy-continuity-cabinet-reshuffle-2026-09-16%2F)

Katayama played a key role negotiating with US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on a rare joint US-Japan yen intervention in late July, ​an effort that underscored the countries' close cooperation.

The reappointment of Katayama, a former finance ministry bureaucrat seen as taking a conservative ​view on fiscal policy, is likely to be welcomed by bond markets wary of Takaichi's expansionary fiscal approach ⁠that could boost debt issuance, analysts say.

"Rather than going for stronger appeal on her policy colour, Takaichi is likely prioritising policy continuity and ​stability to lay the groundwork for re-appointment in the ruling party leadership race in September next year," said Takahide Kiuchi, an economist at Nomura ​Research Institute.

Concern over prospects for Japan's worsening finances has sent the yield on the benchmark 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) to three-decade highs this week, as public debt, at twice the size of its economy, is the largest among advanced nations.

## NO INTENTION OF REINING IN BIG SPENDING PLANS

In a sign that she has no intention ​of reining in her big spending plans, however, Takaichi is also likely to keep her reflationist ally Minoru Kiuchi as economic revitalisation minister, the [Yomiuri](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/japan-pm-retain-kiuchi-economy-minister-cabinet-reshuffle-yomiuri-reports-2026-09-15/) newspaper ​said on Thursday.

Such choices highlight the tricky balancing act Takaichi faces. With households smarting from a rising cost of living, she risks hurting her approval ratings ‌by backing ⁠down on her pledge to cut tax and boost spending.

But she is also under pressure to heed market calls for fiscal discipline, after her ambitious spending plans and a decision to pursue a two-year [tax cut](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/japan-sidestep-funding-tax-cut-outline-keep-fiscal-concern-alive-2026-09-15/) on food items sparked a bond sell-off and [criticism](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/japan-faces-day-policy-reckoning-bessent-calls-time-big-stimulus-2026-09-01/) from Bessent.

Domestic media have said Takaichi is set to retain other key ministers, including some of her competitors in last year's race to lead the ruling party, such ​as Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi and ​Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi.

As head ⁠of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), she also roughly maintained the line-up of party executives on Wednesday in a sign of her focus on political continuity.

Takaichi is expected to give a cabinet post to the ​LDP's coalition partner Japan Innovation Party, looking to solidify the two parties' policy cooperation.

## OPPOSITION SET TO GRILL ​GOVT ON FUNDING

The ⁠new cabinet will head into parliament debate over key fiscal issues such as legislation for a two-year cut in [sales tax](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/japan-sidestep-funding-tax-cut-outline-keep-fiscal-concern-alive-2026-09-15/) on food items, with opposition parties expected to grill the administration over how to fund it.

Takaichi's [pledge](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/japan-aims-cap-fy27-new-bond-issuance-40-trillion-yen-pm-says-yomiuri-interview-2026-08-28/) to cap new government bond issuance around 40 trillion yen ($256.1 billion) for the fiscal ⁠2027 budget ​is already facing scrutiny, with expenditure seen increasing from [budget requests](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/japan-budget-requests-swell-pandemic-era-scale-under-takaichi-agenda-2026-09-04/) that swelled to pandemic-era ​scale.

Japan also faces the prospects of higher defence spending in a strategy review this year.

The cost of funding Japan's debt is increasing as the central bank raises interest rates ​and slows bond purchases in an effort to wean the economy off decades of massive stimulus.

($1=156.1700 yen)

Reporting by Leika Kihara; Editing by Clarence Fernandez

title: Saudi strikes and Houthi attacks widen Middle East war
summary: * Summary * US orders government staff to avoid Yemen border * Saudis say Houthi drone shot down near Mecca * Houthis deny there was an attack there * Houthis say they shot down Saudi fighter * There is no confirmation of this from Riyadh S
content:
*   Summary

*   US orders government staff to avoid Yemen border
*   Saudis say Houthi drone shot down near Mecca
*   Houthis deny there was an attack there
*   Houthis say they shot down Saudi fighter
*   There is no confirmation of this from Riyadh

Sept 16 (Reuters) - Saudi warplanes pounded Yemen and Houthi fighters launched drones and missiles at ​Saudi cities, the Iran-backed movement said on Wednesday, after a lightning advance that has extended Tehran's reach in [the Middle East war](https://www.reuters.com/world/iran/).

In a sign of the worsening ‌conflict in a new theatre, the United States tightened its travel warning for Saudi Arabia, banning government employees from travelling within 20 miles of the Yemen border.

The Reuters Iran Briefing newsletter keeps you informed with the latest developments and analysis of the Iran war. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/reuters-iran-briefing/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fmiddle-east%2Fsaudi-coalition-says-houthi-drone-destroyed-near-mecca-2026-09-16%2F)

The Houthis, who since last week have swept through Yemeni towns along the Red Sea coast and seized islands in the Bab el-Mandeb strait at its mouth, released battlefield video overnight of fighters seizing armoured vehicles from Saudi-backed forces. Warplanes flew overhead and huge explosions billowed into the sky ​from desert dunes, the video showed.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group had launched fresh drone and missile strikes on the major Saudi Red Sea oil port ​of Yanbu, and at a southern Saudi airbase at Khamis Mushait. He did not say when the strikes had taken place. Both cities were ⁠among a wide range of locations where Saudi Arabia announced alerts on Tuesday, although there were no similar announcements on Wednesday.

Saudi officials and oil company Aramco did not immediately respond to ​emails seeking comment.

Earlier, Saree said the Houthis had also shot down a Saudi F-15 fighter jet. No immediate evidence was presented of that incident.

Saree said the Saudis had carried out as many as ​450 air strikes on Yemen this week. Officials in the Saudi-backed government that controls southern Yemen have acknowledged that their forces and those of Saudi Arabia were conducting air strikes on Houthi positions, though Riyadh itself has not confirmed them.

The Houthis have fired repeatedly into Saudi Arabia over the past week causing alarms over cities in the south and west. An attack blamed on Iran-aligned fighters in Iraq last week also knocked out ​Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline, the main route used to divert oil exports from the blockaded Strait of Hormuz.

Riyadh said its air defences had shot down a Houthi drone south of Mecca ​on Tuesday before it entered prohibited airspace over the holy city, an attack it said crossed a "red line" of threatening shrines sacred to all Muslims. Houthi spokesperson Saree denied the group had targeted Mecca, and ‌said the Saudi ⁠reports were a set-up for propaganda purposes.

Item 1 of 2 Iran-aligned Houthi fighters move next to a destroyed vehicle following what the source described as an attack on Saudi-backed forces in the location given by the source as al Jawf governorate, Yemen. HOUTHI MILITARY MEDIA/Handout via REUTERS

**[1/2]**Iran-aligned Houthi fighters move next to a destroyed vehicle following what the source described as an attack on Saudi-backed forces in the location given by the source as al Jawf governorate, Yemen. HOUTHI MILITARY MEDIA/Handout via REUTERS [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/battle-between-iran-aligned-houthi-fighters-and-saudi-backed-forces-in-al-jawf-governate/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMlNKTkFKNFJXWg%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

Sources told Reuters that U.S. officials had held a [meeting with the Houthis](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/us-officials-met-iran-backed-houthis-oman-over-weekend-sources-say-2026-09-16/) over the weekend in Oman, at which the group said it had no intention of attacking American vessels and was committed to a ceasefire reached with the U.S. last year.

## DANGER OF GLOBAL ENERGY SUPPLY SHORTAGE WORSENING

The extension of the war into Yemen threatens to worsen the global energy supply shortage caused by the six-month-old U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, which has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

The price of [Brent crude](https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/oil-falls-us-crude-inventories-rise-despite-saudi-supply-concerns-2026-09-16/) hovered around $108 a barrel on Wednesday , close to its ​highest levels since May. The politically sensitive average ​retail price of diesel fuel in the ⁠United States hit another all-time high above $6.30 a gallon for the first time.

Traders say a prolonged closure of Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline could cut off as much as [4% of global oil supply](https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/saudi-pipeline-outage-threatens-loss-4-global-oil-supply-2026-09-13/). Saudi Arabia has not said when operations might resume, but U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright told ​CNBC on Tuesday that crude oil should be flowing through the pipeline within days.

Saudi Arabia has led a coalition battling the Houthis since ​2015. The conflict had largely ⁠quietened under a ceasefire in recent years, but reignited when the Houthis declared a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia in July and fired at southern areas in the kingdom. Violence has intensified sharply this month when the militant group pushed back forces aligned with the Saudi-backed internationally recognised Yemeni government.

Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman phoned U.S. President Donald Trump last week seeking military support, which so ⁠far has ​been limited to intelligence aid.

The United States bombed the Houthis for two months in 2025, but halted that campaign ​after reaching what President Donald Trump described as a ceasefire that would halt attacks on ships.

Trump now [faces a dilemma](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/houthi-advance-yemen-puts-us-new-bind-2026-09-12/) of whether to stand by and risk the Houthi advance worsening the global energy crisis, or provide more direct military ​support to the Saudis and risk extending the costly U.S. intervention to another theatre.

title: AI发展该放慢脚步或大步前行？美国会两党议员分歧明显

content:
华盛顿 —

近来美国人工智能企业高管频频呼吁放缓AI发展脚步，还有研究人员因担忧AI“可能在十年内毁灭人类”而离职。唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)总统这个星期表示，所谓的“AI末日论”是“骗局”，美国在AI竞争中大幅领先，不应该放慢发展。处在美国政策立法前沿的国会两党议员怎么看？美国之音为您梳理了几位美国政界重要人士的说法。

**特朗普总统：“AI不会接管世界”**

美国总统特朗普9月14日直接打电话给正在洛杉矶参加科技峰会All-in Summit的美国英伟达(Nvidia)首席执行官黄仁勋，黄仁勋打开扩音器让全场聆听。特朗普总统明确地驳斥了所谓的“AI末日论”。他说，“机器人不会接管，人工智能不会接管世界”。他指出整个事件就是场“骗局”(Hoax)。

特朗普总统同一天也在“真相社交”(Truth Social)[发文](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/117269745153543631)表示，“针对人工智能和数据中心有一个病态的阴谋(sick conspiracy)，而唯一会对此感到高兴的是中国。谁掌握人工智能，谁就赢！我们领先于中国和所有其他国家，并将继续保持领先。”

**众议院议长约翰逊：还记得气候变化的夸大警告吗？**

共和党籍联邦众议院议长迈克·约翰逊(Mike Johnson)将人工智能业界发出的警告，和他所说的政治左派对气候变化夸大的警告做对比。

约翰逊说，“当总统说‘骗局’时，他指的是，我们都看过同样的戏码……灾难被制造出来。媒体一片哗然。社交媒体也一片哗然。每个人都在说我们十年内都会死。”

约翰逊的评论看上去指的是纽约州民主党众议员亚历山大·奥卡西奥-科尔特斯(Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez)2019 年刚进入众议院后不久发表的评论，她当时总结了一份联合国关于气候变化的报告：“如果我们不解决气候变化问题，世界将在12年内毁灭。”

他进一步解释：“总统的意思是，你们不会十年内都死去，那就是骗局。”

约翰逊表示，他希望能在本周晚些时候与特朗普总统和人工智能公司高管在白宫进行会谈。

**民主党籍众议员杰弗里斯：国会需立即采取行动**

众议院少数党领袖，纽约州民主党籍众议员哈基姆·杰弗里斯(Hakeem Jeffries)星期一(9月14日)呼吁国会立即采取行动，监管人工智能。

杰弗里斯说，“人工智能的爆炸性增长以及由此而来的挑战--这可不是什么骗局。这非常真实，尽管唐纳德·特朗普对这个问题有不同看法，它需要国会立即采取果断行动，并以目前美国一些领先的人工智能专家所说的方式来做，也就是说，要采取措施放缓发展速度，以保护美国民众的健康、安全和福祉。”

杰弗里斯表示，他在本届国会召集的仅限民主党的人工智能委员会可能很快会开始推出政策建议。“我们希望确保美国创业者和公司能继续在这一领域领先，而不会被中国共产党超越，”杰弗里斯补充说。“但另一方面，我们还必须确保美国民众实际上能够体验到人工智能的好处，而不会受到非常真实、非常严重且非常危险的负面影响。”

不过，杰弗里斯拒绝支持一些民主党同僚提出的建议，也就是如果民主党在11月赢得多数席位，就成立一个专门的人工智能委员会。“我们关注的是实质内容，而不是程序。”杰弗里斯表示，任何关于专门委员会的讨论都将在选举日之后进行。

**民主党籍参议员舒默：警钟比以往任何时候更响**

参议院民主党领袖，纽约州参议员查克·舒默(Chuck Schumer)星期一呼吁，召开一次全体参议员简报会，邀请关键政府官员讨论政府在开发前沿人工智能模型以及阻止中国人工智能发展方面的行动。

舒默说，“我长期以来一直主张，我们必须保持美国在人工智能创新和安全方面的全球领导地位。但这种创新必须伴随严谨的防护措施，以赢得美国公众的信任。警钟比以往任何时候都响得更响--而特朗普政府却视而不见。如果他们自己不承担责任，我们就会承担。如果特朗普不采取行动，国会必须出手。”

舒默表示，参议院有权从政府部门得到三个急迫问题的答复，人工智能的前沿测试框架；对中国的出口管制以及如何防御复杂的人工智能网络攻击。

**参议院多数党领袖图恩：不应将AI未来拱手让给中国**

参议院多数党领袖，南达科塔州共和党籍参议员约翰·图恩(John Thune)星期一表示，美国需要在人工智能领域保持领先，但也需要采取措施应对潜在风险。

在被问到特朗普总统称人工智能威胁是“骗局”时，图恩表示，围绕这个问题有很多“夸张的说法”，但他说：“我一点也不认为我们应该在人工智能方面把未来拱手让给中国或其他任何对手，我认为我们需要在这个领域保持领先，并确保美国人从人工智能中受益。”

图恩补充说：“但我也认为，你必须对人工智能的高级风险系统进行防范。”

**贝森特与民主党籍众议员沃特斯在听证会上的交锋**

加州民主党众议员玛克辛·沃特斯(Maxin Waters)星期二在众议院金融服务委员会上就人工智能问题与财政部长斯科特·贝森特(Scott Bessent)进行交锋。沃特斯表示，总统特朗普“盲目”地推动人工智能模型和数据中心的发展，“完全没有任何保障措施(guardrails)。”

沃特斯追问贝森特，是否看到来自行业领导者包括Anthropic的首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪(Dario Amodei)和微软联合创始人比尔·盖茨(Bill Gates)对人工智能的担忧。

贝森特回复，人工智能公司“想停随时都可以停止”。

他表示特朗普政府“一直在审查”这些模型的前沿。贝森特补充说，政府在“五、六个月前”就开始审查顶级的人工智能模型。

但沃特斯打断了贝森特，并表示，“你的朋友们说要小心，要注意，因为我们正进入人工智能的危险时期。如果你不承认这一点，就意味着你不愿意面对真相。”

贝森特表示，“我们不应该做的是给这些人工智能公司免除责任，这正是他们想要的。保证安全的最好方法就是让创造者对他们制造和生成的东西负责。”

面对科技界发出的人工智能风险警告，美国国会两党议员在“放缓脚步”与“大步向前”之间分歧明显，围绕人工智能相关立法的争论预计仍将在国会山持续。

content:
## Why It Matters

An upcoming House hearing will focus on transnational repression tactics that have moved beyond foreign soil into American communities and universities. The House Foreign Affairs Committee's East Asia and Pacific Subcommittee has scheduled "Lives, Not Leverage: The Long Arm Of China And North Korea's Repression" for September 16.

## Context

According to the [U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission](https://www.uscc.gov/research/chinas-global-police-state-background-and-us-policy-implications), [China operates overseas police stations as part of its transnational repression toolkit](https://www.justice.gov/usao-edny/pr/bronx-man-convicted-operating-police-station-chinese-government-new-york-city-and); conducts intelligence operations targeting Beijing's critics in foreign countries; makes efforts to undermine free speech at universities; engages in online harassment; uses coercion-by-proxy tactics; abuses the INTERPOL red notice system; and leverages extradition treaties. North Korea has strengthened laws to increase citizen reporting of criminal or suspicious activities; increased mass surveillance; and enforces a [shoot-on-sight border order](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2026/country-chapters/north-korea) that originated from a 2020 Covid-19 related decree.

In Hong Kong, the scope of repression has escalated quickly in the five years since the National Security Law was imposed. The territory's last active pro-democracy party, the [League of Social Democrats](https://www.hrw.org/news/2026/02/04/china-repression-deepens-extends-abroad), disbanded in 2025. Authorities used the national security law to prosecute a Hong Kong-based family member of pro-democracy leader Anna Kwok, who is based abroad.

The U.S. has also formally designated the American scholar [U Min Zin](https://www.theepochtimes.com/china/china-accused-of-hostage-diplomacy-ahead-of-trump-xi-summit-6081074), who studies Burma, as wrongfully detained by China.

## The Hearing

[Rep. Young Kim](https://app.legis1.com/lawmaker/detail?id=16857#summary) (R-CA-40) chairs the subcommittee. Human rights activist Deborah Choi is scheduled to testify as a witness.

content:
华盛顿 —

美中领导人峰会举行前夕，一位共和党参议员表示，美中关系目前的核心特征是“竞争”，并强调美国在加强与中国竞争的同时，应降低对中国关键供应链的依赖，并继续支持台湾，同时避免双边关系走向军事冲突。

参议院外交关系委员会东亚、太平洋及国际网络安全政策小组委员会主席皮特·里基茨(Pete Ricketts)星期二(9月15日)在华盛顿智库哈德逊研究所(Hudson Institute)有关美中关系的讨论会上，将这两个全球最大的经济体之间的关系描述为一场长期的战略竞争。

“现在发生的情况是，还有我们目前所处的情况，是一种竞争，”来自内布拉斯加州的里基茨参议员在会上说，“我们需要做的是确保自己不会因在关键矿物、医药前体等物资方面依赖他们，而沦为供应链的人质。”

里基茨表示，中国正在努力降低对美国的依赖，包括发展本土半导体产业、减少对美国食品和芯片等产品的依赖。与此同时，美国也在推动供应链多元化。他认为，美国需要加快这一进程，并争取率先实现供应链调整，以减少中国利用经济依赖对美国施加压力的空间。

“他们正在竭尽全力，确保在食品或芯片等物资方面不再依赖我们。对不对？他们想建立自己的半导体产业，对不对？所以他们正在采取行动摆脱对我们的依赖。我们也在采取行动摆脱对他们的依赖，而且我们必须继续加倍努力，确保率先实现这一目标，这样他们就没有任何筹码来胁迫我们做某些事情，”里基茨说，

他特别强调，美国需要关注关键矿产和药品生产所需原料等领域，避免对单一国家形成过度依赖。

里基茨随后将中国描述为“咄咄逼人、带有恶意的力量”。他说，习近平曾表示，其目标是在2049年前“取代我们”。

“独裁者往往会先告诉你他们打算做什么，然后试图付诸行动，而你必须对此予以高度重视。这就是我们所处的世界，”里基茨说。

不过，里克茨并不主张美中关系完全脱钩。他表示，美中一旦发生战争，将给两国以及世界其他地区带来严重后果。

“我们的目标是避免战争。美国与共产主义中国之间的战争对所有人来说都将是一场灾难，”里基茨说。“正因如此，特朗普总统与习近平主席之间的个人外交是一件好事。我们希望保持这些沟通渠道畅通。我们希望通过对话，让他们理解我们的立场，同时也让我们能更清楚地了解他们的真实想法。”

美中两国元首预计下星期将举行今年第二次高峰会晤。唐纳德·特朗普总统已经确认，中国国家主席习近平将于9月24日到访华盛顿后，白宫将为他举行国宴。这将是继今年5月特朗普开启第二任期首次访华并举行北京峰会后，美中领导人再次会面。

在峰会即将举行之际，里基茨表示，美中对话的一个重要议题应是如何要求中国为美国所指的相关行为承担责任。

里基茨在会后接受美国之音(VOA)采访时表示，在涉及美国国家安全的问题上，美国需要保持高度谨慎。

“此次讨论的一部分内容，必须是探讨我们如何确保让共产主义中国为其恶意行为承担责任，”里基茨对美国之音说，“正因如此，特朗普总统必须非常有力地倡导我们在农业、科技、知识产权盗窃以及威胁我们盟友的恶意活动(例如目前在菲律宾发生的情况)方面所采取的行动。这类的问题太多了。”

农业问题也是里基茨关注的重点。来自农业州内布拉斯加州的他表示，中国过去曾承诺扩大美国农产品进口，但一些承诺并没有得到充分落实。他呼吁特朗普政府要求中国履行相关承诺，为美国农民和牧场主争取更多市场准入。

“我希望特朗普总统采取的行动，也是我们应该做的，就是非常强硬地敦促中国共产党当权者为他们承诺要做的事情承担责任，例如农业方面，”里基茨说。

里基茨同时表示，他对中国履行承诺的意愿持怀疑态度。他说，如果美中峰会能够达成某种协议或妥协，“当然是好事”，但美国在与中国打交道时仍需要保持谨慎。

**里基茨：美国不会改变对台立场**

作为参议院外交关系委员会东亚、太平洋及国际网络安全政策小组委员会主席，里基茨也高度关注台湾议题。他在接受美国之音采访时表示，台湾问题很可能成为美中领导人峰会讨论的议题，并呼吁特朗普在谈及台湾时明确表示，美国的立场没有改变。

“我们不会容忍任何以武力改变台湾现状的行为，”里基茨说。

美国政府目前正在审议一项总额约140亿美元的对台军售计划。特朗普今年5月与习近平会晤后曾表示，对台军售可以成为美国与中国谈判的“筹码”。这一表态引发部分人士对美国对台安全承诺的担忧。

被问及如何看待美国对台军售问题时，里基茨表示，当务之急是尽快向台湾交付已经承诺的武器。

“我认为，重要的是要记住，特朗普总统去年与台湾达成了金额高达110亿美元的最大规模军售协议，而我们在交付武器方面还拖欠了300亿美元，”里基茨说，“因此，让我们把重点放在向台湾交付已经承诺的武器上。这是我们能够采取的、增强威慑力的最好措施。”

里基茨长期支持加强美国与台湾之间的安全和防务合作。2025年5月，他与民主党参议员克里斯·库恩斯(Chris Coons)提出《加强区域伙伴在恶劣环境下防护法案》(PORCUPINE Act)，旨在简化和加快美国对台军售程序。该法案提出将台湾纳入所谓“北约+”类别，从而适用较短的国会通报期限和更高的军售金额门槛，并加快美国及其盟友向台湾转移美国原产军事装备的审批程序。

**美国会放弃第一岛链吗？**

会上，有提问者谈及美国智库“防务优先”(Defense Priorities)近期提出的一项政策主张，即美国应考虑将军事力量从第一岛链后撤至第二岛链，并重新审视与日本、韩国等国的防务联盟。

对此，里基茨当即反问：“他们是拿了中国的钱吗？”这一回应引发现场笑声。

“听起来就像是拿了中国的钱，”里基茨随后说。他认为，如果美国按照中国的核心利益调整自身的军事部署和同盟政策，实际上是在向中国作出让步。

“所以那只是胡说八道，”里基茨直接否定了这一政策主张。

content:
全球约30个推动人权、民主和宗教自由的组织星期三(9月16日)发表致中国共产党总书记习近平的公开信，呼吁他在下星期访问华盛顿之前释放良心犯，承诺停止跨国镇压，并致力于关键司法改革。

这份公开信说：“自从您2012年末掌权以来，我们的组织记录--有些是亲历了--您的政府普遍存在和系统性的人权犯罪，这违反了中国国内和国际的法律义务。”公开信提到习近平政府对藏人、维吾尔人和香港的镇压以及对宗教领袖及社区、女权主义者、新闻记者、律师和公共卫生专家等活动人士的打压。这封信还提到中国新实施的《民族团结进步促进法》。

这些倡导组织还在信中说：“我们与联合国人权专家有着同样的关切，那就是中国各地发生的任意拘押的范围和规模本身可能构成危害人类罪，并与全国各地的受害者及幸存者团结在一起。”

这封信还说：“我们还对您的政府利用跨国镇压和集体惩罚在中国境外压制言论和限制行动感到同样的关切。”公开信提到，这封信的很多签署人就在美国受到过中国政府或中共当局或其代理人的骚扰、跟踪或监视，一些居住在美国的活动人士在中国的家人受到习近平政府的报复。

公开信说：“美国及其他各国政府对这些公然逾越法律的行为进行调查和起诉的努力，令我们深受鼓舞，只要有必要，我们就将继续记录这些侵权行为。”

这封公开信对习近平提出了四点要求：

*   立即并无条件释放良心犯、人权捍卫者以及因其亲属的维权活动而遭任意拘押的人士--其中包括(但不限于)与美国有密切联系且获得美国议员关注的人士：维吾尔族退休医生古丽仙·阿巴斯(Gulshan Abbas)、维吾尔族企业家艾克拜尔·艾赛提(Ekpar Asat)、香港民主派活动人士邹幸彤(Chow Hang-tung)、维吾尔族学者热依拉·达吾提(Rahile Dawut)、中国维权律师丁家喜(Ding Jiaxi)、中国记者董郁玉(Dong Yuyu)、基督教家庭教会领袖高全福(Gao Quanfu)牧师、旅居美国的艺术家高兟(Gao Zhen)、中国维权律师高智晟(Gao Zhisheng)、达赖喇嘛认可的第十一世班禅喇嘛根敦确吉尼玛(Gedhun Choekyi Niyima)、藏族僧侣和作家果·喜饶嘉措(Go Sherab Gyatso)、香港民主派活动人士何俊仁(Albert Ho)、香港民主派传媒大亨黎智英(Jimmy Lai)、香港民主派活动人士李卓人(Lee Cheuk-yan)、缅甸裔美国学者敏辛(Min Zin)、维吾尔族学者伊力哈木·土赫提(Ilham Tohti)、藏族僧人洛桑次仁(Lobsang Tsering)、海外民主运动人士王炳章(Wang Bingzhang)、中国作家和基督徒王怡(Wang Yi)牧师、中国维权人士杨茂东(Yang Maodong)以及基督教家庭教会锡安教会的领袖们。
*   宣布有意废除或修订在习近平领导期间通过的违反国际人权义务的法律，其中包括(但不限于)2020年《香港国安法》和2026年《民族团结进步促进法》。
*   确认允许身处中国境外的人士--包括第十四世达赖喇嘛--在有意前往中国与亲人和社区团聚时能够成行，并确保其行程安全。
*   在抵达美国之前公开确认，中国代表团的所有成员及其在美国的相关人员，将不会针对伴随习近平访问而发生的抗议与抵抗行为，采取跨国镇压或集体惩罚措施。

这封信说，如拒不采取这些行动，习近平的访问只会加深全球公众对中国政府在人权问题上的意图的关切。[公开信](https://freedomhouse.org/article/open-letter-chinese-communist-party-general-secretary-xi-jinping)的签署人还表示愿意有机会在习近平访问期间与他直接会面。

在这封公开信签名的有来自全球倡导人权、民主和宗教自由的各团体的29位人士，其中包括：中国人权捍卫者网络的苏菲·理查森(Sophie Richardson)、哈德逊研究所的奥利维亚·埃诺斯(Olivia Enos)、自由之家的杰米·弗莱(Jamie Fly)、保护记者委员会的马丽怡(Beh Lih Yi)、无国界记者的白奥兰(Aleksandra Bielakowska)、国际特赦美国分会的纳迪亚·达尔(Nadia Daar)、维吾尔国际学院的热沙特·阿巴斯(Rishat Abbas)、世界维吾尔大会的祖姆雷泰·阿尔金(Zumretay Arkin)、国际声援西藏运动的丹曲嘉措(Tencho Gyatso) 、香港自由委员会基金会的马克·克利福德(Mark Clifford)、共产主义受难者基金会的郑国恩(Adrian Zenz)、中国人权与人道中国的周锋锁(Zhou Fengsuo)，等等。

这封公开信的签署者还包括对华援助协会的傅希秋(Bob Fu)牧师。

傅希秋星期三对美国之音(VOA)表示，在习近平十几年的统治下，中国人权、法治和宗教自由状况已经恶化到文革以来最恶劣的状况，全球很多人权工作者感到失望甚至有人绝望，然而他说，即使习近平不会响应公开信的诉求，人权工作者也要借着这次美中峰会的机会，本着良知发声。

他说：“我们不能够因为一个政权的暴力和持续镇压就绝望而沉默。我们反而更应该在这个时刻发出我们的声音。这不仅仅是说我们要评估我们的果效--统治者会不会做出响应的问题，这是我们的道德和属灵的责任，要为那些没有声音的发出声音。”

唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)总统预计将于9月24日会晤来访的习近平。

特朗普总统今年5月在北京与习近平的峰会促成了北京锡安教会领袖金明日(Ezra Jin)牧师的获释，那次元首峰会还提到了黎智英案。

傅希秋表示，如今的中国是习近平一人独尊为大，所以这次美中峰会能不能争取到更多良心犯获释，取决于最高领导人习近平的喜好。

“我不是特别乐观能够释放多人，但是呢，应该在未来的两个礼拜至少做一些友好的表示吧，”他说。

傅希秋牧师说，人权组织几乎已经不抱平反出狱的希望，只是呼吁中国当局考虑到最基本的人道主义底线。

他说：“比如说已经是深度的第四期摄护腺癌症的美国华裔牧师曹三强(John Cao)，他已经服刑七年，过去两年半被释放以来，现在仍关在那边，可以说是在他生命的最后几个月时间，他都不被允许回来美国来跟他的家人团聚。这个无论如何在国际社会上没法做出解释。第二个呢，像高智晟律师，他已经被失踪九年多，死活都不知。目前还是拒绝向家人提供任何信息。还有像王炳章博士。其实很多都是人道的问题。我们基本上放弃说‘把他们平反’甚至‘把他们从监狱释放’。只要有个信息、死活的信息，然后，像曹三强牧师这样，在他临终之前让他跟第一个出生的孙辈见一面，这是多大的奢望呢？”

## 美中峰会前，萧美琴访欧背后的“利基”外交

图像来源，Wang Yu Ching / Office of the President Taiwan

图像加注文字，萧美琴与台湾外交部长林佳龙从意大利返台后，在机场临时记者会向媒体说明欧洲行细节。

*       *   Author, 吕嘉鸿

    *   Author, 李澄欣
    *   Role, BBC中文记者

*   Published 20 分钟前

*   阅读时间: 3 分钟

台湾副总统萧美琴上周现身意大利外海小岛文托泰内（Ventotene），出席欧洲议会主办的自由与民主论坛。

此行发生在特朗普与习近平预定9月底于华府举行峰会的敏感时刻。峰会前，关税与对台军售正是双方谈判桌上持续博弈的筹码。与此同时，身处意大利的萧美琴没有踏入罗马总理府，也未与意大利外长会面，而是走向另一条路径：接受欧洲议会副议长的邀请，现身欧洲议会的场域中。

这场行程刻意保密，直到落地才公开。从台北出发，萧美琴一行辗转搭机、换乘陆路与渡轮，全程耗时约27小时。这种近乎隐蔽的行进方式，也折射出台湾外交处境的艰难：不被联合国承认，在北京持续施压之下，每一步对外接触都需谨慎铺陈。

台北将此行定调为外交突围，北京则痛批为“卑劣且徒劳”。更深的问题是：在中美高层重启接触的缝隙中，台湾尝试藉由欧洲打开外交空间，从去年布鲁塞尔欧洲议会到今年该议会在意大利的活动，台湾试图藉“非主权组织”的邀请，绕开多数欧洲国家的一中政策，突破究竟有多大？

## 北京强硬回应，欧盟降低调门

对此，中国外交部发言人毛宁9月11日在例行记者会上措辞强硬，称民进党当局和个别政客“挖空心思四处蹭热度，打着民主、自由的幌子‘倚外谋独’，这种行为令人不齿、终归徒劳”。毛宁还称，中方已就“台独”政治人物赴意大利出席相关会议，向意大利与欧盟提出严正交涉。

官媒《环球时报》刊出评论称，“真正发生危机时，欧洲政客不会替台湾民众承受断供停产的冲击；美国政客不会替台湾家庭承受战火风险”。

台媒《联合新闻网》则报道，论坛现场原计划悬挂的欧盟委员会标志，在活动当天被撤下。该报引述知情人士称，这显示欧盟委员会不愿因萧美琴到访而影响对华关系。

布鲁塞尔马腾斯中心（Martens Centre）学术委员会成员、曾任欧洲议会政治顾问的冯儒莎（Zsuzsa Anna Ferenczy）向BBC中文表示，萧美琴获欧洲议会副议长接待，凸显议会外交在形塑欧盟与台湾关系上仍具持久重要性。

“在此背景下，欧盟执委会代表取消出席接待萧副总统的活动，令人遗憾，也显得短视。此举可能削弱一场对欧洲具有战略价值的交流，而执委会显然尚未充分认识其重要性。”

北京对萧美琴的批评并不意外。2022年8月，时任台湾驻美代表的萧美琴主导邀请美国众议院议长佩洛西（Nancy Pelosi）访台，事后被中国大陆国台办列入“台独顽固分子”名单。2023年4月，时任台湾总统蔡英文过境美国、与新任众议院议长麦卡锡会面后，国台办再对萧美琴实施“进一步制裁”，禁止她本人及家属进入中国大陆、香港、澳门，并表示将“采取一切其他必要惩戒措施，依法终身追责”。

图像来源，Pina Picierno Meta

图像加注文字，萧美琴是应欧洲议会副议长皮娜·皮齐耶诺（Pina Picierno，右一）与欧洲议会意大利办事处邀请。

## 外交上的“利基”切口

萧美琴虽获欧洲议会邀请，但在接待她的活动中，欧盟执委会代表又取消出席，现场也未悬挂欧盟旗帜，体现出台湾外交空间的狭窄。

但在这样的空间中，仍浮现出一条外交路径：交往对象既不是一个主权国家，而是一个国际组织（即欧盟）；同时也不是其行政分支，而是其立法分支（欧洲议会）。这一双重错位，可以找到一个不容易受到中国压力的外交场域。

确切来说，虽然身处意大利，萧美琴并非受意大利政府邀请，而是应欧洲议会副议长皮娜·皮齐耶诺（Pina Picierno）与欧洲议会意大利办事处邀请，出席第二届“文托泰内欧洲自由与民主论坛”。

文托泰内本身是一个带有历史重量的地点。1941年，反法西斯政治犯曾在这座岛上写下《文托泰内宣言》，后来该文件被视为欧洲联邦主义思想的源头。

台湾大学国家发展研究所助理南乐（Lev Nachman）认为，“即便场域相对利基（niche），正因避开过度挑衅，才让副总统级出访成为可能，仍属有意义的外交开口，也显示副总统不必只坐在台北，而能发挥她最擅长的外交功能。”

“利基”(niche）一词源自法语，原指墙壁上用以放置雕像或装饰品的小凹槽，后来引申为“狭小却精准”的细分市场或特定领域。

这条“利基”路径也有先例。去年11月，萧美琴出席在布鲁塞尔举行的“印太国会议员联盟”年会，也是台湾突破外交孤立的一次尝试——绕过欧盟成员国官方管道，转而透过欧洲议会或跨国议员网络参与价值导向的论坛。

冯儒莎评价称，两次出访表明台湾认真看待与欧洲的关系，并持续投入深化双方伙伴关系。

图像来源，AFP via Getty Images

图像加注文字，中国外交部发言人毛宁则批判萧美琴此行称，“挖空心思四处蹭热度，打着民主、自由的幌子‘倚外谋独’，这种行为令人不齿、终归徒劳”。

## 美中夹缝，台湾的自处与突围

若将萧美琴此行放入中美互动的时间轴来看，台湾议题正成为北京与美方博弈的筹码之一。习近平预计9月24日访问华府，成行前已传出，若美方在峰会前批准对台新一轮军售，不排除取消此次会晤。

在这样的背景下，萧美琴以副总统身份现身欧洲，被外界解读为台湾试图传递“不会被中美接触节奏吞没”的讯号。

冯儒莎向BBC中文表示，除了中国施压之外，当前真正的挑战在于如何缩小“台湾需要欧盟做什么”与“欧盟愿意优先处理什么”之间的落差。她认为，双方都需要更清楚理解彼此利益，并在政治象征与具体实质利益之间取得平衡。

南乐则说，萧美琴此次低调访义，被视为台湾副总统少见的实质外交出击；过往最接近的对照是赖清德赴日参加安倍国葬，但层级与性质不同。她行前保密到家，抵达文托泰内后才曝光，发言务实克制，符合其长年外交官风格。

至于把此行解读成牵制特朗普与习近平的会面，南乐认为两者几乎没有连动，属一厢情愿之说。“北京最在意的仍是对台军售。”

但作为欧洲学者，冯儒莎同时强调，欧洲自身面对的挑战或许更大：“欧洲必须更坚定地界定自身利益、捍卫自身战略空间，并在外部行为者试图干预其内部事务时予以反击。归根究柢，问题不只是欧洲愿意为台湾走多远，而是欧洲是否愿意为自己发声。”

_This article is published as part of ‘The World Tomorrow’, the magazine’s new strand for fresh ideas about the direction of global order._

On 18 October 2017, delegates at the Chinese Communist Party’s National Congress listened to their leader announce a new political doctrine, ‘Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era’. It discussed party discipline, national security and the direction of travel for China, among other topics. But as Xi outlined his doctrine for a de facto new state ideology, he also expressed something that none of his predecessors, not even Chairman Mao, attempted: a global strategy for China based primarily on his own thought.

It was a remarkable moment in the history of Communist China’s foreign policy. In late 1978, Deng Xiaoping ushered in China’s ‘reform and opening up’ era. In the three decades that followed, China’s foreign policy adhered to another dictum of his – that China should ‘hide its capabilities and bide its time’. His successors Jiang Zemin and Hu Jintao largely did just that, shying away from anything approaching a global strategy. This approach served China well as it led to western policymakers helping China to modernize and emerge as a potential superpower.

## Xi Jinping Thought

That all changed with Xi Jinping Thought. Since taking office in 2012, Xi had consolidated power; but it wasn’t until his speech on the eve of his second term that he defined more clearly ‘the China Dream of National Rejuvenation’, with his vision of consolidating the party’s control over everything as an instrument for China to forge a ‘common destiny for humankind’ by 2050.

> Recent American administrations have made the mistake of thinking that China wishes to replace the United States as the global hegemon.

It set out Xi’s plan to return China to global preeminence. Xi believes such preeminence will emerge if China can pull off a double pivot in its global strategy: establishing its leadership of the Global South and gaining control of Taiwan. The two are inextricably linked with his ambition, ultimately, of transforming the world order. Yet as important as it is to understand these goals, it is equally important to grasp Xi’s approach to foreign policy – something that the United States and other western powers often fail to.

A conventional ‘realist’ assessment of China’s foreign policy emphasizes its national interest and its power relative to other nations. Xi and his regime certainly make those calculations. Yet, such an assessment risks failing to see that Xi’s ideological preferences and the security of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) trump all other considerations in Beijing’s global strategy. This makes China under Xi an unusual kind of realist actor, one which I and Olivia Cheung examine in our new book _China’s Global Strategy under Xi Jinping_ – the term we use for Xi’s vision is ‘Sino-centric party state realism’.

—
China’s leader Xi Jinping, left, with President Abdel-Fattah el-Sisi of Egypt upon his arrival in Cairo on 1 September, 2026. Key to Xi’s global strategy is his influencing of Global South countries. Photo: Khaled Desouki / AFP via Getty Images.

An understanding of what Sino-centric party state realism means for China’s global ambitions is crucial for western powers seeking to compete with and challenge Beijing. Many fail to apprehend the true nature of these ambitions. For instance, recent American administrations have made the mistake of thinking that China wishes to replace the United States as the global hegemon and impose a new world order. That isn’t the case, as I’ll argue below.

It is also necessary to recognize that Beijing has no interest in enabling us to understand China’s global strategy – its interest is in getting us to understand it in ways that benefit China. But first, it is helpful to examine a key concept in this strategy.

## A ‘common destiny for humankind’

In the CCP’s official English translation of this concept in Xi Thought, the Chinese leader sees across the world an opportunity to build ‘a community with a shared future’. This phrase is routinely repeated by western policymakers, analysts and news media. It is an anodyne statement, deliberately so, and, arguably, framed to disarm and mislead. A faithful translation of the Chinese is ‘a common destiny for humankind’, which reveals a more concerning vision. A ‘common destiny’ for all does not emerge organically in a community of free and equal agents choosing to share a future; it needs to be forged by a leader, China.

> A ‘common destiny’ for all does not emerge organically – it needs to be forged by a leader, China.

How might China forge this ‘common destiny’? By, in Xi’s words, the ‘democratization of international relations’. In this framing, China is not seeking to replace the existing international order or the US as the global hegemon with the legacies that would entail, such as undertaking the role of the world’s police officer. Instead, Xi’s ambition is for China to take over the leadership of the international order by securing the support of the Global South, thereby executing its first pivot.

Global South countries represent a clear majority in the UN General Assembly and by population count. The modified order would be Sino-centric, based on Xi’s understanding of the traditional Chinese concept _tianxia_ (see sidebar at foot of the article) – in theory at least, a fundamentally different model of global leadership to the American-led rules-based order.

To expedite this ‘democratization’, China does not work to export its Leninist political system; rather, China’s aim is to help countries of the Global South resist the US and the West imposing their liberal-democratic political model on them. In pursuit of this goal, Xi has deployed enormous diplomatic and economic resources.

Since 2021, he has announced four global initiatives, on development (2021), security (2022), civilization (2023) and governance (2025), complemented by the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI), China’s global infrastructure and economic development strategy. In this process, China’s relations with the US have been relegated to a lower priority, contradicting the belief in Washington that Beijing is fixated on outcompeting Washington. Instead, Beijing pursues its global ambition by cultivating support from the Global South, which is defined loosely to include almost every nation outside the ‘democratic West’. By this formulation, when Chinese preeminence is accomplished the end of US hegemony is simply a by-product.

## Wooing the Global South

Xi’s four global initiatives have attracted relatively little attention in the West. The US and Europe are not the intended audience. But the initiatives do appeal to the weaker democracies and autocratic regimes of the Global South whose leaders appreciate that Xi’s suite of initiatives not only commits China not to interfere in their domestic affairs but also gives them protection against others – the US and its allies primarily – from doing so. For example, at the Boao Forum of April 2021, Xi said: ‘We must not let the rules set by one or a few countries be imposed on others, or allow unilateralism pursued by certain countries to set the pace for the whole world.’

This is why many Global South leaders understand the Chinese rhetoric of the ‘democratization of international affairs’ implies a transformation of the international order from one imposed by a self-righteous and democratic US, as they see it, to a more hands-off alternative shaped by authoritarian China.

—
A TV news report broadcast in a restaurant in Taipei, Taiwan, shows the meeting between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in Beijing in May. Xi told the US president their two countries should be ‘partners not rivals’. Photo: I-Hwa Cheng/ Getty Images.

The attraction is reinforced by China’s offer of otherwise unavailable development loans without conditionalities such as accountability and transparency, via the BRI scheme. The scaling back of the BRI in recent years may have reduced the size of these loans but it remains substantial at close to $124 billion for 2025. The refined approach has made Chinese development projects more sustainable and subject to less abuse, without significantly reducing their value in cultivating support.

The other demand Beijing makes of Global South countries is to give verbal support for its claim over Taiwan, which is cost-free to them. Little wonder that Xi’s global initiatives gain traction in more and more Global South countries.

> Beijing is asking Global South countries to give verbal support for its claim over Taiwan, which is cost-free to them.

China has also used the support of Global South countries to expand and consolidate its control over important parts of key international organizations, of which the most important is the United Nations. For example, at the United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs and the Human Rights Council, Beijing, with support from its Global South partners, has fundamentally changed how they operate and made them responsive to Chinese preferences in the past two decades.

In this way, Beijing is building momentum for further changes within the UN, at a time when most western democracies are neglecting it and reducing their overseas development budgets. The unrelenting enhancement of Chinese influence at key international organizations is meant to enable China to make more decisive changes when it is ready.

## The Taiwan pivot

The second pivot in China’s global strategy is to take Taiwan, in defiance of the US commitment enshrined in its Taiwan Relations Act (1979) to help the country defend itself against an externally imposed change in its status. Taiwan matters not so much because it is the top producer of critically important advanced microchips but because it lies in the middle of the strategically vital First Island Chain in the Pacific Ocean and has only remained beyond Chinese control thanks to US protection.

> If achieved, the taking of Taiwan, and the discrediting of the US in the process, would mark China’s assertion of its global preeminence.

In Beijing’s approach to Taiwan, Xi has made a paradigm shift. To all his predecessors, including Mao, Taiwan was unfinished business from the Chinese Civil War (1946–1949), but none saw a need to specify a timeline for its incorporation into China. In contrast, Xi has made Taiwan central to his China Dream of National Rejuvenation, making 2050 the deadline for taking it.

Beijing’s preferred outcome is to demonstrate overwhelming military superiority that pressures Taipei to submit to ‘reunification’ and thus remove the American raison d’être for intervention. Should this tactic fail, it will use force. The calculation is that success by either means will reveal US impotence to counter a spectacular Chinese move to take control of the First Island Chain. That would not only enable China to project power deep into the Pacific but would force key US allies such as Japan and South Korea to calculate if they can still rely on their respective defence treaties with the US for their security.

If achieved, the taking of Taiwan, and the discrediting of the US in the process, would mark China’s assertion of its global preeminence. Crucially, it would link the dual pivots of its global strategy, ushering in an appeal to China’s supporters in the Global South to make significant changes to key international organizations.

The first “China shock” was fairly easy to understand. Beginning in the 1990s, cheap Chinese goods poured into global markets, displacing large parts of lower-end manufacturing across the world. Now, [China shock 2.0](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/diplomacy/article/3355120/european-leaders-get-ready-act-now-amid-rising-fears-china-shock-20?module=inline&pgtype=article) seems to be under way, with China taking the lead in electric vehicles (EVs), batteries, solar panels, semiconductors and other more technologically sophisticated industries.

This is often perceived as a trade problem, with Chinese manufacturers producing too much, selling too cheaply and [flooding global markets](https://www.scmp.com/week-asia/economics/article/3277522/southeast-asias-struggle-stay-afloat-amid-flood-cheap-chinese-imports?module=inline&pgtype=article) with subsidised goods. However, the more consequential question is not just why the United States and Europe run growing trade deficits with China. It is who is supplying the next round of industrial growth in Asia, Africa, Latin America and other emerging markets. That makes today’s industrial competition more of a production story than a trade story.

Headlines on the technological race between China and the US are usually about the frontier: [artificial intelligence](https://www.scmp.com/topics/artificial-intelligence?module=inline&pgtype=article) (AI), advanced semiconductors, quantum computing, biotechnology and other fields in which scientific leadership could determine the future. China’s efforts to catch up with the technological and productivity frontier can make it look like the country’s industrial future lies entirely at the highest end of technology.

However, much of China’s industrial expansion is happening in a different area: technologies that are less cutting edge but already proven and widely used throughout the world.

Much of the modern economy does not run on frontier technology. Rather, it relies on mature technologies that are reliable, affordable and fit for the job. China is becoming one of the main suppliers of that kind of proven technology.

Automobiles show why industrial competition is not just about the frontier. German industrial strength has never depended on producing every German car inside Germany. By 2010, German carmakers were already producing more vehicles abroad than at home. Much of the production shift has been visible in China and the so-called German-Central European supply chain.

Volkswagen employees work on the assembly line for its ID.3 electric car at the company’s “Transparent Factory” production site in Dresden, eastern Germany, on May 14, 2025. Photo: AFP

China presents a different challenge. It is not that German manufacturers are incapable of producing electric cars; Germany still remains a major EV producer. Rather, electrification has changed the source of much of the value, technology and strategic dependence. While the internal combustion vehicle rewarded decades of German expertise in engines, transmissions and mechanical engineering, EVs rely more heavily on batteries, semiconductors, software and digital architecture. Germany might still produce EVs, but a growing share of the components on which those cars depend now comes from China.

The EV race is not just about having the latest technology. China’s battery dominance has been built in large part around [lithium iron phosphate](https://www.scmp.com/business/companies/article/3154120/how-do-electric-vehicle-batteries-work-and-why-do-they-sometimes?module=inline&pgtype=article) technology, a mature technology that is cost effective, reliable and suitable for mass-market vehicles.

Automobiles also depend on mature chips. A Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago report estimates that an average internal combustion vehicle contains more than 1,000 semiconductors, around 95 per cent of which are mature or legacy chips. EVs use more sophisticated processors, but they still rely heavily on mature chips alongside other proven technologies such as batteries, software and digital architecture. These are precisely the areas in which China has built a dense domestic ecosystem.

The semiconductor industry consists of much more than frontier processors. China’s share of global capacity for mature chips has expanded dramatically: it has grown three to four times during the past decade, rising from about 17 per cent in 2015 to 33 per cent in 2024 and a projected 45 per cent in 2027. Such chips will not power the most advanced AI models or [graphics cards](https://www.scmp.com/tech/tech-war/article/3310317/nvidias-consumer-graphics-cards-see-price-hikes-china-after-h20-sales-ban?module=inline&pgtype=article), but they do perform many of the less spectacular but key functions without which the modern economy cannot operate.

China [subsidising its industries](https://www.scmp.com/economy/china-economy/article/3167588/chinas-industrial-subsidies-what-are-they-and-why-are-they?module=inline&pgtype=article) is far from a new development, and the use of subsidies, tax incentives and below-market borrowing are hardly unique to China. What makes China different is partly where the money has gone.

Financing technology-intensive industries does not necessarily mean financing only the most cutting-edge technologies. In fact, much of China’s capital is going into technologies that are already mature. Since 2021, China’s semiconductor industry has made more than US$75 billion in new investment, primarily in legacy technology nodes. China is competing in the race for advanced chips, but it is also pouring capital into the less glamorous technologies on which much of the industrial economy already depends.

The central story is that the modern industrial economy does not simply replace mature technologies with frontier ones. Mature technologies are not obsolete technologies. They are becoming increasingly important to China’s position in the global industry as machinery, electrical equipment and transport equipment now account for more than half of the country’s exports. China is also exporting more of these products to emerging markets, [especially within Southeast Asia](https://www.scmp.com/economy/global-economy/article/3360517/chinas-power-exports-asean-surge-40-first-half-2026-amid-hormuz-tensions?module=inline&pgtype=article).

Now, the US and European responses to China still focus on controlling what enters their markets, but the deeper challenge is production capacity. Tariffs might keep some Chinese goods out of American or European markets, and export controls might slow China’s progress in some frontier technologies. However, neither does much to prevent Chinese machinery, components and capital goods from replacing Western products in emerging markets.

The key question is not simply who invents the technologies of tomorrow; it is who produces, adapts and scales the mature technologies that the modern economy already runs on today. A country can remain at the scientific frontier while losing the ability to manufacture the technologies that support it.

China’s manufacturing model makes one thing clear: industrial competition requires both innovation at the frontier and the ecosystems needed to produce proven technologies that support the industrial economy.

title: China Confirms Large Scale Buildup of Silo-Based Strategic Nuclear Forces
summary: China has for the first time provided a semi-official acknowledgment of its significant investments in expanding its silo-based intercontinental-range ballistic missile arsenal, after work on this was first observed in commercial satellite
content:
China has for the first time provided a semi-official acknowledgment of its significant investments in expanding its silo-based intercontinental-range ballistic missile arsenal, after work on this was first observed in commercial satellite imagery in 2021. A new CCTV documentary marking the 99th anniversary of the People’s Liberation Army features a PLA engineer discussing his work constructing what he describes as “houses for missiles” in remote mountains and deserts. The documentary links the work of PLA engineer First Master Sergeant Cui Daohu to the construction program, and describes considerable pressure from senior leadership to complete it on schedule.

Final Stages of DF-5B Silo-Based Nuclear Missiles

The three principal fields, located near Yumen in Gansu Province, Hami in Xinjiang and Yulin near Ordos in Inner Mongolia, contain approximately 320 suspected ICBM silos. The Yumen field contains about 120 silos, Hami approximately 110 and Yulin around 90. Before the discovery of the fields, China maintained a comparatively small silo-based ICBM force alongside road-mobile missiles. The construction programme has therefore been assessed as the largest expansion of China's nuclear arsenal to date. The silos are distributed across enormous areas of China's interior. The Yumen field covers approximately 1,110 square kilometres, Hami approximately 1,030 square kilometres and Yulin approximately 830 square kilometres.

DF-31 Nuclear ICBMs

The silos are generally separated by several kilometres, complicating efforts to destroy multiple launch sites with a limited number of weapons. The locations are also considerably deeper inside China than most of the country's older ICBM bases. One of the most significant aspects of the new documentary is its description of the urgency surrounding construction. Cui said he was repeatedly questioned about whether the project would be completed on time and described developing faster construction methods to meet the deadline. He linked the project to the need to ensure that China could retain its strategic deterrent capability.

B-21 Strategic Bomber Prototype - USAF

The ability to neutralise China’s ground-based nuclear forces is considered a primary requirement for the U.S. [B-21 strategic bomber program](https://militarywatchmagazine.com/article/us-surges-production-b21-200-pacific-war), which was designed to launch penetration strikes into heavily defended airspace. The rapid expansion of China’s nuclear deterrent complements major investments in strengthening the country’s air defences, which is expected to make the destruction of its nuclear forces on the ground far less viable. The naval and air arms of the Chinese nuclear triad are also being improved significantly, most notably with the Type 096 ballistic missile submarine program, and at least one [intercontinental range stealth bomber](https://militarywatchmagazine.com/article/first-clear-look-china-intercontinental-stealth-bomber) program.
